headline: Bus fares rise by 17 paisa per km after fuel price hike
summary: Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam warns bus operators that charging passengers above the government-fixed rates will lead to route permit cancellations.
details: Following a Tk 20-per-litre increase in fuel prices, the government has decided to raise bus fares by 17 paisa per kilometre.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam warned bus operators that they could have their route permits cancelled if they charge passengers more than the fixed fares.
The minister stated that there are provisions for fines and that future issuance of route permits to offenders may be reconsidered.
Transport owners had initially demanded a 20-paisa-per-km hike along with adjustments for higher maintenance costs due to the rising dollar rate.
The government kept the hike below the requested rate after lengthy discussions to reduce the pressure on the general public.
Regarding other transport, the minister said no decision has been taken to increase railway fares, and he will make every effort to ensure they remain unchanged.
Freight transport leaders were also instructed to follow the rules, while launch fares will be reviewed following further discussions with owners.
caption:
Bus fares are going up. The government has fixed a 17 paisa per km increase following the latest fuel price hike.

Following a Tk 20-per-litre increase in fuel prices, the government has decided to raise bus fares by 17 paisa per kilometre.

Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam warned bus operators that they could have their route permits cancelled if they charge passengers more than the fixed fares.

The minister stated that there are provisions for fines and that future issuance of route permits to offenders may be reconsidered.

Transport owners had initially demanded a 20-paisa-per-km hike along with adjustments for higher maintenance costs due to the rising dollar rate.

The government kept the hike below the requested rate after lengthy discussions to reduce the pressure on the general public.

Regarding other transport, the minister said no decision has been taken to increase railway fares, and he will make every effort to ensure they remain unchanged.

Freight transport leaders were also instructed to follow the rules, while launch fares will be reviewed following further discussions with owners.

headline_marked: Lawmaker's wife [[sent to jail after remand]] in suicide abetment case
headline: Lawmaker's wife sent to jail after remand in suicide abetment case
summary: The first wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam has been jailed after providing information during her one-day remand.
details: The first wife of Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam, Maksuda Begum, has been sent to jail following a one-day police remand.
The case involves the alleged abetment of suicide of the lawmaker's second wife, Mariam Khatun, whose body was found hanging from a flat in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.
The investigation into the case has been handed over to the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
A Dhaka court had previously granted four days' remand for Gazi Nazrul Islam and one day for Maksuda Begum.
The case was filed by Mariam's father, Masum Billah, who accused the lawmaker and two others of abetting his daughter's death.

Gazi Nazrul Islam was expelled from Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on July 22 after an internal investigation found evidence of 'moral misconduct' following the social media circulation of certain video clips.
caption:
A lawmaker's first wife is in jail after her second wife was found dead. The DB is now leading the investigation.

The first wife of Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam, Maksuda Begum, has been sent to jail following a one-day police remand.

The case involves the alleged abetment of suicide of the lawmaker's second wife, Mariam Khatun, whose body was found hanging from a flat in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.

The investigation into the case has been handed over to the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

A Dhaka court had previously granted four days' remand for Gazi Nazrul Islam and one day for Maksuda Begum.

The case was filed by Mariam's father, Masum Billah, who accused the lawmaker and two others of abetting his daughter's death.

Gazi Nazrul Islam was expelled from Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on July 22 after an internal investigation found evidence of 'moral misconduct' following the social media circulation of certain video clips.
